data.name: An Oath to the Stars
data.detailed_description:
Left for dead by her closest friend and comrade, Hoshiko is now looking for revenge.
Follow her in this modern hardcore danmaku SHMUP about revenge, friendship and honour.

Features:

  • Action packed SHMUP action - Brought to you by long-time genre lovers.
  • Distance Overdrive - Get close to enemies and use your laser to deal more damage and gain faster kills.
  • Momentum Combo - Increase your combo gauge killing enemies as fast as you can.
  • Four Difficulty levels, from the accessible Easy to the super-challenging Inferno Mode.
  • Dozens of controllers supported, including Dual Shock 3 and 4, Xbox 360 and One, Wii GamePad Pro, multiple Arcade Sticks, and Keyboard support.
  • Local multiplayer
  • Full Control mapping
  • TATE Mode
  • Online Leaderboards and Achievements

reviews.review:
[h1]Overview:[/h1]
'[i]An Oath to the Stars[/i]' is a top down bullet hell shoot'em up where you play as Hoshiko, a mech fighter that gets betrayed by a comrade by the name of Chiyoko. There are also cutscenes that give the player more substance to the story and what happened to Hoshiko but despite this, no [i]real[/i] explanation as to why the betrayal took place is given. Fight through 5 levels where you attempt to track down and exert your revenge on your traitor, each with their own unique boss. I love bullet hell games and am I huge fan of the [i]Touhou[/i] series but '[i]An Oath to the Stars[/i]' feels inconsistent and unfair on many planes. Imagine playing through this just to receive a half-assed cliffhanger ending.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
By no means is '[i]An Oath to the Stars[/i]' easy nor is it meant to be. Difficulty can be good [i]when[/i] done right but it isn't here. There's a difference between something being hard and something being impossible. '[i]An Oath to the Stars[/i]' adopts many bullet hell elements but does not use these elements correctly. Bullet hell games for one have patterns that the player can learn and adapt to even if it's difficult. However over half of the enemy bullets in the game don't have a pattern and are for the most part scattered and give no room or information for the player to squeeze through or dodge. More times than one I die then come back to a barrage of bullets I can't dodge because there's no conceivable pattern for me to read and possibly dodge as there are bullets going in literally every direction.

There's also a secondary attack in the form of a laser that supposedly does exponentially more damage than your regular attack but I honestly see little to no difference between the two besides the fact that the laser is limited. The game states that the laser does more damage point blank but when I think about it, there's almost no instances where you'd ever be in the position to take advantage of that. The only useful time I can imagine using the laser is on a laser enemy or a boss, but the issue lies in being able to close the distance with all the random bullets flying every which way, it's just a death wish and makes more sense to kill them the traditional way. Another feature tossed out the window.

Another thing is how the bullets are implemented. Fast, swerving bullets are one thing. But if you throw hundreds of them at the player along with clusters of bullets from other enemies, no human can realistically dodge them unless they position and move themselves in a very specific pattern beforehand (assuming they know exactly what's coming). It's not intuitive and is just a cheap death after another. There are other times where there is literally no time for the player to react to the incoming stream of bullets or lasers before they inevitably explode. This happens in both regular combat as well as some boss battles. There's just [b]no[/b] room to vacate time to react to any attacks sometimes because the boss is too big or the onslaught of bullets make no viable sense.

In addition, there are no last resort mega bombs, shields, or movement slowing features either. Just raw move and shoot. For bullet hell games, this is ludicrous. The inability to have even the slightest bit of defensive or agile help in a game all about dodging bullets is truly hardcore and I commend anyone able to feasibly beat these levels on the harder difficulties without help on top of ridiculously impossible to dodge bullets that have no pattern. The overall level design is just terrible and done poorly for what bullet hell games are supposed to be and I honestly never thought 5 levels would be such a nightmare to play through (but for the wrong reasons).

[h1]Controls:[/h1]
All it is is move and shoot. Again, extremely lacking for a game in this genre. This is definitely a game where people deserve medals if they can beat it.

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]
Meh at most. Colourful sure but the vibrant colours can sometimes obscure the bullets coming towards you. Despite them only being one of two colours, it doesn't help that both the background and bullets can blend well together. The rest of the game has a more cartoon-ish take and isn't bad but could be better. Enemies including bosses all resemble a specific art style as well and get old quickly. There's no enemy variety and many enemies end up repeating in later levels making gameplay repetitive, but we're not talking about that here.

[h1]Audio:[/h1]
Also limited. As mentioned, you're fighting the same types of enemies so you end up only hearing a specific few sound effects. The music is your typical mix of high hype shoot'em up music and is nothing memorable or unique.

[h1]Conclusion/TL;DR:[/h1]
'[i]An Oath to the Stars[/i]' is a top down bullet hell shoot'em up with terrible level and boss design that proves difficult to play but for the wrong reasons. Lacking features that normal bullet hell games have (movement slowing, defensive abilities), '[i]An Oath to the Stars[/i]' is truly a game for the most hardcore of hardcore bullet hell gamers, those looking for games that offer little to no avoidable patterns to overcome and want an unfair shooting game to play that has death around every corner.
